chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Muhammad ibn Marwan from the Sheikh (peace be upon him)
That Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) died and left sixty slaves, so he freed one-third of them. I cast lots among them and freed the third.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams handle the manumission of multiple slaves according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam al-Baqir’s (AS) specific legal methodology for manumission, illustrating the Shia juristic principle of using lots (qur'a) to select slaves for freedom when a fixed portion is designated. It highlights the practical application of wills (*wasiyya*) regarding slaves, a key topic in *fiqh al-man* (jurisprudence of slaves), and reflects the Imam’s role in clarifying procedural details of inheritance and emancipation. The act of freeing one-third aligns with the general Islamic rule of disposing of up to one-third of an estate in a will, ensuring the rights of heirs are preserved.
